papers.title: Integration of AI and Geophysical Sensing for Environmental Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with geophysical sensing provides a scalable and data-driven solution for environmental risk assessment. This study presents a supervised machine learning framework designed to classify environmental risk levels (low, medium, and high) using statistical features extracted from simulated geophysical signals.
papers.methodology: Synthetic geophysical signal simulation, statistical feature extraction using mean, standard deviation, and RMS, 70:30 stratified train-test split, optional SMOTE class balancing, and Random Forest classification.
papers.dataset: 500 simulated geophysical signal samples with approximately balanced Low, Medium, and High risk classes.
papers.findings: The Random Forest model achieved approximately 76% accuracy on the reported testing dataset. The paper also reports accuracy exceeding 85% in balanced scenarios and above 90% in optimized configurations using data balancing techniques.
